newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-DETTORI MAKES HISTORY WITH 25,095-1 SEVEN-TIMER.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DETTORI MAKES HISTORY WITH 25,095-1 SEVEN-TIMER.

text.p: Champion jockey Frankie Dettori blazed into the record books on Saturday, winning all seven races on the card at cumulative odds of 25,095-1.
Dettori took the opening day of the big two-day autumn festival by storm and cost the bookmakers millions in the process.

The history-making successes were on Wall Street (2-1 favourite), Diffident (12-1), Mark of Esteem (100-30), Decorated Hero (7-1), Fatefully (7-4 favourite), Lochangel (5-4 joint favourite) and Fujiyama Crest (2-1 favourite).
The feat surpassed all others and brought a big crowd to its feet as Dettori booted home his last winner, making all the running and holding on narrowly to win by a neck.
Ex-champion Willie Carson had six winners from seven rides in an afternoon at Newcastle in 1990. In 1957 Alec Russell rode all six winners at a minor meeting in Scotland.
But to achieve seven out of seven underlined the charisma of of the ebullient Italian-born jockey, one of the most popular sportsmen in Britain.
Dettori said: "It's been an incredible day -- a dream come true." He added: "I definitely feel lucky. I must do the lottery tonight."
His many big race wins include the 1996 St Leger on Shantou and last year's Prix de l' Arc de Triomphe on Lammtarra.
But he found himself on another star on Saturday in Mark of Esteem, who he had partnered to win the 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket.
In the Queen Elizabeth 11 Stakes, Mark of Esteem proved himself Europe's top miler with a stunning victory.
Dettori took up the running in the final 200 metres to sprint home one and a quarter lengths clear of 1,000 Guineas winner Bosra Sham, trained by Henry Cecil and ridden by Pat Eddery.

Dettori said of the 100-30 winner: "I`ve never had that feeling in my life. It was such a quality race yet he was going so easily with a furlong (200 metres) left. He's got to be an exceptional horse. He's undoubtedly the best miler I've riddden."
French 2,000 Guineas winner Ashkalani, who started 9-4 favourite, finished only fifth.
Mark of Esteem's victory, worth over $310,000, may have effectively clinched the 1996 trainers' championship for Saeed Bin Suroor who handles the Godolphin horses for Sheikh Mohammed of Dubai.

Ironically, it was a dispute last year over Mark of Esteem which led to a split between Cecil and Sheikh Mohammed and ended with the sheikh withdrawing his horses, including Mark of Esteem, from the trainer's Newmarket yard.
